title: Jahanabad Buddha
subtitle: Manglawar rock relief up the Malam Jabba road, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Jahanabad Buddha
edits: The rock is the Atlas's procedural model: a tall granite face about 9 m wide, 12 m high and 8 m deep, its carved front kept vertical; the dark streaks, the lumps and the three boulders beside and behind it (4-7 m) are estimated from the photos, not a survey.

The Buddha in relief is drawn to the published size of 700 x 500 cm (Wikipedia): the source does not say which side is the height, so it is taken as 7 m high and 5 m wide. The same article also quotes 'the colossal image of a seated Buddha some thirteen feet in height' (about 4 m); that figure is not reconciled and is not used. The throne is 120 x 390 cm (1.2 m high, 3.9 m wide), and the oval niche, its 0.3 m depth and the relief standing 0.11 m proud of the niche floor are estimated; the folds, hands, head and halo are estimated from the published description and the photos.
The figure's foot is set 1 m above the ground at the face (estimated).

Trees within 25 m of the carving are left out so it can be seen; WorldCover maps tree cover there. A timber viewing deck (3.6 x 1.0 m, 0.3 m high) at the foot of the face is estimated from the photos.
No steps are mapped in OSM and none show in the photos, so none are drawn; the walk up from the road is traced over the ground (easiest slope on the DEM).
The carving is drawn restored and without the 2007 damage to the head.

sources.name: Buddhist rock carving in Manglawar (Wikipedia)
sources.use: size of the Jahan-Abad-i relief (700 x 500 cm, asana 120 x 390 cm), its orientation (facing north west), its 2007 damage and restoration

osm_use: the Malam Jabba Road (S-15) to the point where the mapped departure to the Buddha begins, and the Buddha node
